PART 1 - USER MANUAL EXCERPTS
1.1 WP-400 CNC Panel Saw (Woodworking)
Section 1.1.1 Daily startup procedure
Doc ref: UM-WP400-1.1.1  |  Category: Machine Operation Issues  |  Machine: WP-400
1. Check the compressed-air gauge. Working pressure must read 6.0 bar (0.6 MPa). Do not start below 5.5 bar.
2. Inspect the main saw blade for missing teeth, cracks or resin build-up. Replace a damaged blade before use.
3. Turn the main isolator to ON. The controller boots in about 45 seconds.
4. Press HOME. All axes (X, Y, blade height) must complete homing without alarm.
5. Start the dust extraction. The blade cannot start while extraction is off (interlock).
6. Load a cutting program and run one test cut on scrap before production.

Section 1.1.3 Dust extraction
Doc ref: UM-WP400-1.1.3  |  Category: Machine Operation Issues  |  Machine: WP-400
Minimum air velocity at the saw hood is 20 m/s. The controller raises alarm E-102 when the filter pressure drop
exceeds 1200 Pa. Clean or replace the filter cartridge WP4-FL-DE1 when the alarm appears. Never bypass the
extraction interlock.

1.2 SC-900 Bridge Saw (Stone)
Section 1.2.1 Startup and water supply
Doc ref: UM-SC900-1.2.1  |  Category: Machine Operation Issues  |  Machine: SC-900
1. Open the water supply valve. Minimum flow is 8 L/min at 2 bar. Never run the blade dry.
2. Confirm the flow indicator on the operator panel is green.
3. Clamp the slab and check that it is fully supported underneath.
4. Switch on the spindle and wait 10 seconds for full speed, then lower the bridge.

section: Section 1.2.2 Making a straight cut in slab
text:
Section 1.2.2 Making a straight cut in slab
Doc ref: UM-SC900-1.2.2  |  Category: Machine Operation Issues  |  Machine: SC-900
Set the blade depth 5 mm below the slab thickness. Recommended cutting speeds: granite 30 mm at 1.2 m/min,
marble 30 mm at 2.0 m/min. For slabs thicker than 40 mm make two passes of equal depth. Slow down when the
blade exits the slab to avoid chipping the underside.

1.3 MC-250 CNC Plasma Cutting Table (Metal)
Section 1.3.1 Startup and gas supply
Doc ref: UM-MC250-1.3.1  |  Category: Machine Operation Issues  |  Machine: MC-250
The plasma supply needs clean, dry compressed air at 6.2 bar (90 psi). Drain the filter bowl daily. Attach the work
(ground) clamp directly to clean bare metal on the plate; paint and rust prevent a stable arc. Switch on the power
source, wait for the READY lamp, then home the torch height controller (THC).

Section 1.3.2 Cut settings
Doc ref: UM-MC250-1.3.2  |  Category: Machine Operation Issues  |  Machine: MC-250
Pierce height is 3.8 mm and pierce delay 0.4 s for mild steel. The THC arc-voltage target is 125 V.

1.4 GC-120 Automatic Glass Cutting Table (Glass)
Section 1.4.1 Loading and scoring
Doc ref: UM-GC120-1.4.1  |  Category: Machine Operation Issues  |  Machine: GC-120
The GC-120 handles sheet glass 3-12 mm thick. Set the scoring pressure for the thickness: 4 mm = 2.2 bar, 6 mm
= 3.0 bar, 10 mm = 4.2 bar. Keep the cutting-oil level above the MIN mark. Vacuum pressure must read at least
-0.6 bar before scoring.

Section 1.4.2 Break-out and edge quality
Doc ref: UM-GC120-1.4.2  |  Category: Machine Operation Issues  |  Machine: GC-120
Break the sheet within 30 seconds of scoring; the score line loses effect as the glass relaxes. A clean score is thin
and continuous. Shells or flares along the edge mean the wheel is worn or the pressure is too high.

Section 2.4 Ordering parts and warranty
Doc ref: MP-ALL-2.4  |  Category: Maintenance & Parts  |  Machine: All
Order parts through your authorised distributor and quote the machine model, serial number and part number from
Section 2.3. Wear parts (blades, electrodes, nozzles, scoring wheels, filters, belts) are consumables and are not
covered by warranty. Other replacement parts carry a 12-month warranty from the invoice date. Standard parts
ship within 5 working days; diamond blades and spindle bearings may take up to 10 working days.

PART 4 - RESOLUTION PROCEDURES
SAFETY: Before any maintenance or blade/consumable change, switch the machine off, lock out the main
isolator per your site lock-out/tag-out procedure, and wait until all moving parts have stopped.

section: Section 4.1 Replace the WP-400 saw blade
text:
Section 4.1 Replace the WP-400 saw blade
Doc ref: RP-WP400-4.1  |  Category: Technical Troubleshooting / Maintenance & Parts  |  Machine: WP-400
1. Switch off and lock out the machine. Wait 2 minutes until the spindle has fully stopped.
2. Open the blade guard and insert the spindle lock pin.
3. Remove the arbor nut. The WP-400 arbor nut has a left-hand thread.
4. Remove the outer flange and old blade. Clean both flanges and the arbor.
5. Fit new blade WP4-BL-300 with the rotation arrow matching the spindle direction.
6. Refit the outer flange and tighten the arbor nut to 60 Nm.
7. Remove the lock pin, close the guard, remove lock-out, run at 1000 rpm for 30 seconds, then at full speed.
8. Reset the blade-hours counter. If E-206 returns, re-inspect the flanges for damage or debris.

section: Section 4.2 Replace the SC-900 diamond blade
text:
Section 4.2 Replace the SC-900 diamond blade
Doc ref: RP-SC900-4.2  |  Category: Technical Troubleshooting / Maintenance & Parts  |  Machine: SC-900
1. Switch off, lock out, and close the water valve. Raise the bridge fully.
2. Lock the spindle and remove the flange bolt.
3. Remove the flange and blade. Check flange faces for burrs; runout limit is 0.1 mm.
4. Fit the new blade with the arrow in the direction of rotation. Tighten the flange bolt to 80 Nm.
5. Open the water, confirm 8 L/min, and run without cutting for 1 minute.
6. Make a first cut at half the normal feed to bed in the blade. Dress with an abrasive block if it glazes.

Section 4.3 Replace MC-250 torch consumables
Doc ref: RP-MC250-4.3  |  Category: Technical Troubleshooting / Maintenance & Parts  |  Machine: MC-250
1. Switch off the power source and disconnect it from the supply; shut off the air.
2. Unscrew the shield cap, then remove the nozzle, swirl ring and electrode in that order.
3. Replace the electrode if the pit is 1.5 mm deep. Always fit a matched set (electrode, nozzle, swirl ring, shield).
4. Lightly coat O-rings with silicone grease only. Do not use petroleum grease.
5. Refit parts hand-tight; do not use tools on the nozzle or shield.
6. Restore air at 6.2 bar and make a test cut on scrap.

section: Section 4.4 Replace the GC-120 scoring wheel
text:
Section 4.4 Replace the GC-120 scoring wheel
Doc ref: RP-GC120-4.4  |  Category: Technical Troubleshooting / Maintenance & Parts  |  Machine: GC-120
1. Switch off and lock out the machine. Move the scoring head to the service position.
2. Remove the retaining screw and take out the old wheel.
3. Fit a new wheel GC1-SW-6 and refit the screw finger-tight plus a quarter turn.
4. Switch on, check scoring pressure for the thickness, and make a test score on 4 mm scrap.
5. Break the test piece within 30 seconds. The edge should be clean without shells.

Section 4.5 Recalibrate the WP-400 Y-axis
Doc ref: RP-WP400-4.5  |  Category: Technical Troubleshooting  |  Machine: WP-400
1. Make sure rails are lubricated (grease LG-2) and the table is clear.
2. Home all axes, then open Diagnostics > Axis Calibration.
3. Make a 1000 mm test cut on scrap panel.
4. Measure the cut with a calibrated rule and enter the measured value.
5. Accept if the deviation is within 0.2 mm over 1000 mm. Otherwise repeat once; if it still fails, check the Y-axis
belt and encoder cable.

PART 5 - FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
Doc ref: FAQ-ALL-5  |  Category: Mixed  |  Machine: All
[WP-400] Q: Why do I get E-101 right after restarting the compressor?
A: The tank is still filling. E-101 clears when pressure rises above 5.5 bar; wait and press RESET.
[WP-400] Q: How often should I change the saw blade?
A: Typically every 80-120 operating hours, or sooner if edges chip. See the parts table in Section 2.3.
[WP-400] Q: Can I run the saw with the extraction off for a quick cut?
A: No. The interlock prevents blade start and bypassing it is not permitted.
[SC-900] Q: Can I use dirty or recycled water?
A: Only if it is filtered. Blocked water filters cause alarm F-01; clean SC9-WF-02 weekly.
[SC-900] Q: How do I know the diamond blade is worn out?
A: Segment height below 3 mm, or the blade cuts slowly even after dressing.
[MC-250] Q: Why does my plasma arc go out halfway through a cut?
A: Usually a poor ground connection, rust or paint on the plate, or speed set too high.
[MC-250] Q: Which consumables should I keep in stock?
A: At least two sets of electrode MC2-EL-65, nozzle MC2-NZ-65, swirl ring MC2-SW-65 and shield MC2-SH-65,
plus a spare air filter MC2-AF-10.
[GC-120] Q: Why does the glass break away from the score line?
A: A worn wheel, low scoring pressure, or waiting more than 30 seconds before breaking.
[GC-120] Q: Which oil should I use in the scoring head?
A: Use GC1-OL-1L cutting oil only and keep the level above MIN.
[All] Q: Are blades and nozzles covered by warranty?
A: No. They are consumables. Other parts have a 12-month warranty (Section 2.4).
